# Decisions

## C1 - SLA clock for P1

**Decision:** We have decided to measure the SLA clock for P1 incidents using absolute wall-clock time (24/7), ignoring standard business hours.

**Rejected alternative:** Pausing the SLA resolution clock outside of regular business hours (using a business-hours-only clock).

**Reason:** Priority 1 incidents represent critical system outages that require immediate attention regardless of the time of day to minimize massive business disruption.

**Service owner:** Chief Information Officer (CIO) or VP of IT Operations, because they are responsible for overall system uptime and critical incident response protocols.

**Customer outcome:** Customers receive immediate, round-the-clock resolution for critical issues, ensuring maximum availability of key business services.

## C2 - Closed tickets and reopening

**Decision:** Closed tickets will remain strictly immutable and cannot be reopened by reporters or agents under any circumstances.

**Rejected alternative:** Allowing reporters or support agents to reopen previously closed tickets if they feel the issue is not fully resolved or if it recurs.

**Reason:** Forcing a new ticket for recurring issues ensures accurate tracking of resolution metrics, prevents SLA manipulation, and maintains a clean audit trail.

**Service owner:** ITSM Process Manager or Service Desk Manager, as they define ticket lifecycles, SLA auditing rules, and overall reporting standards.

**Customer outcome:** The organization benefits from accurate reporting and clearer audit trails, while users are assured that a recurring issue is treated as a fresh incident with its own SLA.

## C3 - VIP reporters and the priority matrix

**Decision:** VIP reporters will automatically have their tickets escalated to the highest priority, overriding the standard impact and urgency matrix.

**Rejected alternative:** Strictly adhering to the standard impact and urgency priority matrix for all users, without any exceptions for VIP status.

**Reason:** Executive leadership and key stakeholders require expedited support to ensure their operational bottlenecks are removed immediately, reflecting their high business value.

**Service owner:** Director of Customer Support or Service Delivery Manager, as they manage client relationships, business expectations, and define support tiering levels.

**Customer outcome:** High-profile VIP users receive expedited, white-glove support, minimizing downtime for key decision-makers and high-value personnel.
